art.title: The Dance Class
art.holder: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
art.story: A ballet class at the Paris Opéra is nearly over. The old teacher, the famous dancer Jules Perrot, leans on his cane and taps the floor, while one girl performs and the rest are tired: they stretch, fiddle with their hair, scratch their backs, sit on the piano. A big mirror on the wall shows the room. Degas did not paint the glamour of the stage but the hard work behind it, in tutus and ballet shoes. He returned to dancers again and again, more than to any other subject.
